name: ddl_bulk_first_5
notes: q_ddl M01 — BULK-before-LAT discriminator. One 5-request async batch (2 writes + 3 reads, all nr=8). Classification (q_ddl.bpf.c:104-118): writes -> BULK lane; nr=8 reads -> LAT lane. Fresh burst: requests are microseconds old, so rule 1 (LAT 1ms deadline missed), rule 2 (BULK 10ms starvation) and rule 3 (200us guard) are all cold; dispatch precedence (q_ddl.bpf.c:170-227) rule 4 (BULK pending) outranks rule 5 (LAT pending): ISSUE order = BULK lane arrival FIFO [4608, 3072], then LAT lane arrival FIFO [5120, 3584, 2560]. Discriminates q_ddl from BOTH q_mq_deadline behaviors: C-LOOK would issue sector-ascending [2560,3072,3584,4608,5120]; mq-deadline read-first would lead with reads. BULK count kept at 2 (<=3) so the BULK drain stays microsecond-scale and rules 1-3 stay cold (determinism). Sectors 2560..5120: above the partition-scan zone (0..2048), same validated family as mqdd_rev_5, no power-of-two sector, same-op start-to-start spacing >=512 sectors (write gap 3072->4608=1536; read gaps 2560->3584=1024, 3584->5120=1536) — plug merge immune (q_ddl allow_merge=false additionally kills scheduler-queue merges, bpf.c:340-344).
